title: interactive handoff cards with anchored provenance and elapsed-timer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: oncall handoffs are noisy and fragile—important context gets lost when responders paste ad-hoc notes or attachments. This PR introduces an interactive, compact handoff card UI and server-side representation that attaches a tamper-evident provenance token, an elapsed-timer anchored to the incident start time, and an optional severity-delta field to communicate how the oncall perceives trend since the last handoff. Goals: reduce cognitive load during handoff, make provenance auditable, and provide a small, copyable payload for downstream automation (pager bridges, runbook runners).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new handoff-card server model (handoff/cards.go) that stores summary, anchored_provenance_token, incident_start_ts, timer_offset_sec, severity_delta, and sanitized_attachments metadata. Tokens are HMAC-SHA256 over canonical handoff fields with key rotation hooks.
- Exposes a small REST endpoint POST /api/v1/incidents/:id/hands that accepts compact JSON and returns a canonical card payload and short-lived attachment URLs.
- Implements interactive web component src/ui/handoff-card.tsx which renders the compact card, starts a live elapsed timer calculated from incident_start_ts + timer_offset_sec, and provides copy-to-clipboard (compact JSON) and 'attach sanitized snippet' flows.
- Adds CLI helper cli/handoffctl (subcommand 'card create') for engineers to create cards from terminals and include sanitized logs via --snip.
- Adds audit logging and wire-level TTL: cards are immutable once created and tokens expire after default 30 days; attachments default to 72 hours.
- Adds unit + e2e tests and docs for runbook integration.

Implementation notes:
- Security: anchored_provenance_token uses a server-side HMAC key stored in KMS; the code includes rotate_provenance_key() with a migration path so old tokens remain verifiable. Tokens do not expose secrets and are small (base64).
- Performance: payloads are intentionally compact; the UI requests only metadata for the last 25 handoffs on the incident list to avoid heavy payloads. Attachments are stored in the existing ephemeral-bucket service; we reuse the signed-url pattern.
- Rollout plan: feature gate off by default. Console feature flag `handoff_cards_v1` added. We will enable for 10% of incidents, monitor oncall latency and card-create errors.

Files changed (high level):
- server/handoff/cards.go (new): model + HMAC helpers
- server/handoff/handlers.go: controller wiring and validation
- migrations/20260210_add_handoff_card_table.sql: DB migration
- src/ui/handoff-card.tsx: new interactive component + styles

- ephemeral-bucket/integration.go: TTL handling for signed URLs (small refactor)
- test/e2e/handoff_card_flow.test.ts: end-to-end coverage for create/list/copy
- docs/handbook/handoff-cards.md: usage, security notes, rollout checklist

Review thread (selected):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice ergonomics. Two asks: 1) can we keep the card payload <1KB by default (avoid embedding snippets)? 2) ensure the timer is timezone-agnostic and always anchored to server incident_start_ts to avoid client clock skew issues."
- Maya (author): "Agree on size constraint—attachments are only metadata + signed URL, snippets are uploaded separately. Timer uses server timestamp and client uses local monotonic timer after initial delta. Added unit tests to validate clock-drift tolerance (see commit 4)."
- Nina Shah (security): "Provenance token looks fine but we need KMS key rotation docs and audit linkage. Also add an explicit expiration claim to the token to prevent reuse."
- Maya: "Added rotate_provenance_key() and documented the verification fallback for previous key IDs. Token now encodes expiry (exp) and a key_id. Updated docs and added audit log entries in handlers."
- Roberto Kim (qa): "e2e was flaky around signed URL expiry in test environment; tests assume 72h TTL and CI mock used 1h. Please parameterize TTL in test fixtures."
- Maya: "Fixed tests to parametrize TTL via test config; CI uses short TTL to exercise refresh logic."

CI summary: initial run had a lint failure (UI styling variable); second run failed one flaky e2e related to signed-url mocking; third run passed all checks. Checks run: unit tests (server), ui-tests (lint + jest), e2e (playwright), security-scan. All green on final run.

Migration & compatibility: The migration adds a new table handoff_cards and backfills nothing. Existing oncall flows are unchanged. Feature is behind flag so no runtime impact until enabled. There is a small DB index added on incident_id + created_at to keep list queries fast.

Telemetry / observability: New metrics exposed: handoff.card.create.count, handoff.card.create.latency_ms, handoff.card.copy.count, handoff.card.attach.upload_errors. Alerts: handoff-card-create-error-rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers paging to infra. Dashboard: added compact handoff card panel to oncall console (per-incident).

Release notes (short): "Add interactive handoff cards with anchored provenance tokens and elapsed-timer to improve oncall handoffs; feature is feature-flagged and off by default."

Merge details: merged via squash on 2026-02-15 after final approval from Diego and Nina. Post-merge: feature flag created, doc entry added to runbook, and a 10% rollout scheduled for 2026-02-22.
